propositions: Tests lacking subprocess return-code checks or timeout budgets escape CI detection, resulting in flaky or long-running test suites that burn resources; 27 defects in fortnight review were absent-oracle tests or timeout-budget violations.

Ruff linting lacks PLW1510 (subprocess-run-without-check) and eleven PT codes across 481 findings tree-wide in src/, tests/, and scripts/; these codes are not selected in [tool.ruff.lint] and are absent from local make lint runs.

Per-test timeout enforcement exists only in CI workflows (--timeout=300/120 via command line) and uses thread method, but local pytest runs have no per-test budget, leaving test regressions undetected until CI.
Four existing @pytest.mark.timeout marks and two hygiene scripts (check_wall_clock_asserts.py, check_raw_git_writes.py) are unreachable from make lint, running only in CI workflows.

Adopting the selected ruff codes, ini-level pytest timeout with func_only override, marking integration tests that exceed budget, and wiring hygiene checks into make lint requires updates across config, CI workflows, test marking, and documentation without removing existing hang guards.
